mechanism: Reformation's Protestant challenge provoked the Catholic Counter-Reformation, whose patronage and propaganda drove the dramatic, emotive Baroque style.
Late Mannerist painters' artificial, elongated forms evolved into the Baroque's dynamic naturalism and theatrical drama in Italy around 1600.
Critics in France promoted Classicism's order and restraint as a reaction against the excesses of Baroque ornament.
Polarization and clashes over the Second Spanish Republic's reforms pushed the military rebels under Franco to launch the 1936 coup.
Depression-era unemployment and economic hardship deepened class conflict and radicalized Spanish politics before the war.
Franco's Nationalist victory in 1939 installed a dictatorship that governed Spain as Francoist Spain until 1975.
The Sui dynasty's collapse after failed Korean campaigns and rebellions let the Li family found the Tang dynasty in 618.
Tang's collapse after 907 fragmented China into the Five Dynasties and Ten Kingdoms period of rival regional regimes.
Caesar's victory in the civil war gave him the dictatorial authority to overhaul the Roman calendar, producing the Julian reform of 46 BC.
Germany's defeat and the Allied victory in World War I forced the Paris Peace Conference to impose the 1919 treaty on Germany.
Taoist alchemists under Tang patronage experimented with saltpeter, sulfur and charcoal, producing the earliest gunpowder formulas.
Song-era Chinese engineers packed gunpowder into projectiles, producing early explosive bombs that spread the military use of the powder.
Abbasid propagandists and Khurasani armies overthrew the Umayyads in the 746-750 revolt, establishing Abbasid rule in Baghdad.
Umayyad rule had become unpopular with non-Arab Muslims and Shia, and its defeat at the Zab in 750 ended the dynasty.
Abbasid patronage at Baghdad, including the House of Wisdom, drove translation and scholarship that defined the Islamic Golden Age.
Babur defeated the Lodi sultan at the First Battle of Panipat in 1526, founding Mughal rule over northern India.
Mughal decline after Aurangzeb's Deccan wars let Maratha leaders build a rival state that contested Mughal power across India.
After Mughal authority fragmented in the eighteenth century, the East India Company used rival successor states to extend British control over India.
Faraday's 1831 discovery of electromagnetic induction showed that a changing current in one coil induces current in another, the principle of the transformer.
Electromagnets developed in 1825 gave experimenters a controllable magnetic field, which Faraday and Henry used in their induction apparatus.
Declaring independence from Britain in 1776 led the states to write the 1787 Constitution, which created the federal government in 1789.
Fighting in Donbas during 2014 led Ukraine, Russia and separatist representatives to sign the Minsk Protocol ceasefire in September 2014.
The Yugoslav Wars dissolved the federation, leaving Serbia and Montenegro as the rump Yugoslav state formed in 1992.
NATO's 1999 bombing campaign over Kosovo weakened Milosevic's regime and pushed the rump federation toward the 2003 restructuring under EU mediation.
Luigi Galvani's 1786 experiments on animal electricity led Alessandro Volta to build the voltaic pile, the first true electric battery, in 1800.
Steady currents from voltaic cells let Oersted and later researchers study electricity and magnetism, opening the field of electrical science.
Early electric motors of the 1830s were powered by battery cells, so their practical operation depended on batteries.
Surrealism grew directly out of Dada's anti-art revolt in Zurich and Paris, and Andre Breton's circle absorbed Dada's members and methods.
The trauma and disillusionment of the First World War led artists like Breton and Ernst to reject rational order and explore the unconscious.
Germany's defeat in the Second World War and the Allied occupation created the western zones that became the Federal Republic in 1949.
The Potsdam Conference fixed Germany's division into Allied occupation zones, the administrative basis for the separate West German state.
Soviet rejection of Western plans for a unified Germany and the emerging Cold War pushed the Western zones toward a separate state.
West Germany was a founding member of the European Economic Community, whose 1957 Treaty of Rome was negotiated with Adenauer's government.
Shortly after the 1960 ruby laser, researchers used laser pulses to measure distances and particles in the atmosphere, creating lidar in 1961.
The 2003 invasion of Iraq destabilized the region, and the resulting sectarian and jihadist networks later fed Syria's armed uprising.
Amid the collapse of Assad's authority in 2012, Kurdish forces in northern Syria seized territory and built the autonomous Rojava administration.
Alexander Fleming's wartime treatment of infected wounds in 1915-18 convinced him antiseptics failed, prompting his search for natural antibacterial agents.
The Second World War left millions of children displaced and starving, and the UN General Assembly created UNICEF in 1946 to aid them.
UNICEF helped draft the 1989 Convention on the Rights of the Child and now monitors and promotes its implementation in member states.
Soviet domination of postwar Eastern Europe after the Second World War set up the communist states that Moscow bound into the Warsaw Pact in 1955.
Enlightenment thinkers' belief in disseminating useful knowledge inspired Scottish printers in 1768 to produce Britannica as a general encyclopaedia.
Japanese woodblock prints imported to Paris in the 1860s showed Monet, Degas and others flat colour, cropped composition and sketch-like brushwork.
Impressionism's break with academic painting and its focus on light and modern life helped launch the Post-Impressionist and modern art movements.
Germany's defeat in the First World War and the collapse of the Kaiserreich left a discredited government and set up the republic's founding in 1918-1919.
The November 1918 revolution forced Kaiser Wilhelm II to abdicate and let Social Democrats proclaim a republic, which the Weimar constitution then formalized.
Harsh reparations and territorial losses in the 1919 treaty fed nationalist resentment that undermined Weimar's legitimacy from the outset.
The Weimar Republic's collapse in economic crisis and political deadlock brought Hitler to power in January 1933, creating Nazi Germany.
Activists used Twitter and Facebook to coordinate protests and circulate footage of police repression, accelerating uprisings in Tunisia and Egypt in 2011.
Chapter XIV of the Charter established the International Court of Justice as the principal judicial organ of the UN, which began sitting in 1946.
The Charter's human-rights commitments led to the Universal Declaration of 1948 and the 1966 covenants, including the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights.
Enlightenment ideals of reason, tolerance and sociability spread through European lodges, and the 1717 London Grand Lodge set up Freemasonry as a formal institution.
Improved optical microscopes let Jan Swammerdam and later observers see individual blood corpuscles, allowing red blood cells to be identified in 1658.
Industrial-era mechanization and precision metal production made practical needle-and-shuttle mechanisms possible, leading to the first sewing machines around 1790.
Precision lathes and machine tools produced the metal parts, cams and gears that early sewing machine designs required.
The October Revolution of 1917 put the Bolsheviks in power and created the Russian SFSR as the Soviet state's core republic.
Defeat and economic collapse in the First World War weakened the Russian Empire and opened the way for the 1917 revolutions that created the RSFSR.
The RSFSR was the largest constituent republic of the Soviet Union formed in 1922, and it dominated the federation's politics and economy.
Integrated circuits packed many transistors onto one chip, letting microprocessors be built cheaply enough for affordable personal computers in the 1970s.
Transistors replaced vacuum tubes in computer logic and memory, making machines smaller and more reliable, a precondition for desktop computers.
Enlightenment ideals of public access to knowledge and systematic collecting shaped the 1753 Act that founded the British Museum as a public institution.
Zeno of Citium taught Stoicism in Athens during the Hellenistic period, when Greek philosophy had spread across the Mediterranean and the Near East.
After the 1857 Indian Rebellion, Parliament dissolved the East India Company's rule in 1858 and placed India directly under the British Crown.
Britain's 1947 transfer of power, with its communal electoral legacy, led to the partition of British India into India and Pakistan.
British forward policy in Afghanistan, driven by Raj fears of Russian influence, provoked the Second Anglo-Afghan War of 1878-1880.
Ardashir I exploited decades of Roman-Parthian warfare and Parthian fragmentation to overthrow the Arsacid dynasty and found the Sasanian state in 224.
The Congress of Vienna in 1815 merged the former Austrian Netherlands with the northern Dutch provinces under William I, creating the kingdom.
The Napoleonic Wars ended French rule in the Low Countries and restored the House of Orange, which the 1815 settlement then made into a kingdom.
Italian Futurists adopted Cubism's fragmented planes and overlapping viewpoints to depict motion and speed in their own paintings from 1911.
Art Deco designers drew on Cubism's geometric simplification and angular stylization, which became central to the style's decorative vocabulary.
Freud's psychoanalytic accounts of the unconscious and dream life gave modernist writers and painters a new model of subjective experience.
Surrealists carried modernism's experimental break with realism forward, using the unconscious and chance to dissolve conventional representation.
Dada's anti-art provocations in Zurich extended modernism's rejection of inherited artistic conventions into open attacks on bourgeois culture.
Morse's telegraph receiver worked by an electromagnet pulling a stylus, so an electromagnet was the core device that Morse's dots and dashes drove.
Voltaic batteries supplied the steady current that Morse's 1830s telegraph needed to send signals over wire between stations.
Philip II's centralizing Catholic policies and taxes in the Netherlands provoked the Dutch revolt that became the Eighty Years' War against Spain.
Spanish claims to newly discovered lands after Columbus's voyages led Spain and Portugal to divide the New World by the 1494 Treaty of Tordesillas.
